contract.direct_answer:
To resolve a list of gene symbols to verified ENSDARG IDs, each symbol must be looked up against the authoritative identifier resolver — Ensembl Zebrafish (Danio rerio), which the evidence bundle explicitly names as "the authoritative identifier resolver behind the DATA INAMOVIBLE" (ZFIN can supplement with synonyms/mutant/marker cross-references). The correct procedure is: (1) submit every symbol to the Ensembl Danio rerio resolver, (2) accept the returned ENSDARG only when there is an exact, unambiguous match, and (3) emit a POSITIVE NOT_FOUND flag for any symbol that returns no match, an ambiguous/multiple match, or only a deprecated/withdrawn ID. A positive NOT_FOUND is itself a valid, informative result — it must be asserted, not silently dropped.

IMPORTANT: This evidence bundle does NOT contain the actual list of gene symbols to resolve, and "Key entities resolved in DI: (none checked)" — meaning no symbol was actually verified against Ensembl here. Therefore I cannot output any specific ENSDARG IDs. Doing so would violate the core rule.

Why IDs must never come from memory: (a) A language model's recalled ENSDARG strings are unverifiable and frequently hallucinated or outdated — Ensembl IDs are versioned and periodically retired, merged, or reassigned, so a "remembered" ID may point to the wrong gene or no gene at all. (b) Zebrafish nomenclature is riddled with paralogs (ohnologs, e.g. -a/-b duplicates), synonyms, and symbol reassignments, so a symbol→ID mapping is only trustworthy when read live from the authoritative store (Ensembl_DanioRerio, cross-checked in ZFIN). (c) The whole DATA INAMOVIBLE design treats Ensembl as the single source of truth precisely so that every asserted identifier is auditable against the verified store; an ID from memory cannot be audited and breaks that guarantee. Hence: resolve live, bind every symbol to its checked ENSDARG, and flag unresolved symbols as NOT_FOUND rather than inventing an ID.
